title: What If You Flew a Spaceship Through Saturn's Rings?

scenes.text: What if you flew straight through Saturn's rings? They aren't what they look like.
The rings stretch over 170,000 miles across, yet are often only about 30 feet thick.
Up close they aren't solid at all. They're countless chunks, from dust specks to house-sized boulders.
Almost all of it is water ice, which is why the rings shine so bright.
Scale the rings down to a sheet of paper, and they'd be over a hundred times thinner.
A disc wider than the planet's whole span, thinner than a three-story building. Cross it, and you'd be through in moments.
